name: nm47
question: Does nm25 re-trained against a more aggressive rule pool (two maniacs, a bigger pool share, a larger and faster-restarting exploiter), the recipe nm46 ran by hand, pass nm45's checks when its checks are fixed before it trains?
why: nm46 was trained by hand on 2026-11-24 (results/ninemax/nm46_byhand/): nm25's recipe started from nm25 with the pool maniac, maniac, tag, station, reg at share 0.6 (nm25: reg, reg, tag, maniac, station at 0.5), exploiter share 0.35 restarted every 45 minutes (nm25: 0.25, 60), snapshots every hour. Run afterwards through nm45's checks it passed every one that finished: against the station +1.15 [+0.58, +1.71] vs nm25 where nm45 was -16.53, against the maniac +0.92 [+0.57, +1.28], reg and tag level, 25 styles mean -0.03 and worst -1.38, no-harm -0.23 over 40,000 deals, all three bluffers lose. Those checks were chosen after it trained, so they describe it and cannot adopt it; this run repeats the recipe with its checks set first. Same GPU as nm46 (the 3090), so the hand count matches.

checks.why: it must not lose to nm25 in nm25's own game

nm45's check, unchanged: on the same deals as nm25, the 95% interval of the difference must lie above -2.0 bb/100 against every rule player. More maniacs in training must not cost the station win nm44 and nm45 lost
at least as good as nm25 on average across 25 generated players, and never far behind (as nm45)
bluff jams and raises must lose prize equity against it, as against nm25
as nm45: the mean of four 30-minute exploiters, limit nm25's +0.75 plus 0.5. The check most at risk: nm46's first seed read +1.0
a report for the reviewer: where nm47 decides differently from nm25
